Parliament No:2
Session No:1
Volume No:28
Sitting No:7
Sitting Date:18-12-1968
Section Name:BUDGET
Title:BUDGET, FIRE BRIGADE
MPs Speaking:Mr Chan Chee Seng (Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social Affairs); Mr Ng Yeow Chong; Mr P. Coomaraswamy (Mr Speaker);


Column: 601



    Mr Ng Yeow Chong: Mr Speaker, Sir, I beg to move,

    That the sum to be allocated for Head 1103 be reduced by $10 in respect of subhead 2005.

    Sir, I note that there is a tremendous increase in the amount for this vote for the next financial year as compared with the provision for last year. As explained in the Memorandum on the Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure, the increase is due to the payment of rental of all the fire hydrants in the Republic to the

Column: 602

Public Utilities Board. From now on theP.U.B, will be responsible for the installation of new hydrants and for the maintenance of existing ones as well as for the cost of water supply to these fivehydrants. Sir, our Fire Brigade is known to be among the best equipped -

    Mr Chan Chee Seng: It is the best!

    Mr Ng Yeow Chong: Yes, it is the best equipped. It is the most efficient Fire Brigade in this part of the world. Yet, many people in Singapore do not appreciate its excellent and efficient service. They often blame it for not being able to control the big fires that broke out in certain slum areas.

    The Chairman: Mr Ng, you will have to speed up a little.

    Mr Ng Yeow Chong: I wish to refute this allegation. I contend that if it had not been for the efficiency of the Fire Brigade, the fires in the squatter areas would have affected the adjacent built-up and developed areas. It must be admitted that fire fighting in certain slum areas is extremely difficult because of the congestion of squatter houses and the lack of fire fighting facilities, such as fire hydrants. The recent fire at Bukit Ho Swee nearly threatened a block of Housing Board flats which were adjacent to the area under fire. The Fire Brigade was able to check the fire from spreading to the adjacent developed areas. Therefore, I wish to pay a tribute to the Fire Brigade and its members for their high efficiency.

    In connection with fire hydrants, may I ask -

7.50 p.m. .

    The Chairman: Order. I am afraid we have reached "guillotine" time. As the Question has not been proposed, no question of withdrawal arises.
